How it works

From your payments to your money back.

Upload an export of your payments. Reclaim checks every one, shows you the records behind each result, and helps you get the money back once you confirm it. Nothing reaches a vendor until you approve it.

Step by step

Six steps, from a CSV to money back.

Step 1 of 6

Upload your payments

Export your payments as a CSV from QuickBooks Online, Xero, BILL, NetSuite or a spreadsheet. Our guides show which reports to run. Then log in, click Upload a ledger and drop the file in.

Step 2 of 6

Reclaim checks every payment

It compares each payment with the ones around it, looking for duplicates, overpayments, missed discounts, changed bank details and unusual amounts. The checks run right in your browser.

Step 3 of 6

You see the proof

Each finding shows the vendor, the amount and the exact payments behind it, with the matching details highlighted. A flag isn’t money owed. It means something is worth checking.

Step 4 of 6

You confirm it’s real

A few plain questions check the finding against your bank and your bills: did both payments clear, has a credit already covered it? Then you mark it real, ask for more detail, or dismiss it.

Step 5 of 6

You approve the request

Reclaim drafts the request from the records. You set the amount, choose a refund or a credit, and edit the message. Nothing goes out until you approve it, and you send it from your own email.

Step 6 of 6

You track it until the money lands

Recoveries shows where every request stands and when to follow up. You log the vendor’s replies, and money only counts as recovered when it actually comes back.

Questions

The questions people ask first.

  • What records does Reclaim need?

    Your bills, the payments against them, your vendors, and your vendor credits. You upload them as CSV exports. Our export guides show where to find them in common accounting tools.

  • Do I need to connect my accounting system?

    No. You can start with files you export yourself. QuickBooks direct import has a sandbox adapter and requires separate authorization.

  • What does Reclaim look for?

    Eight things: exact and near-duplicate payments, overpayments, invoice numbers shared across vendors, changed vendor bank details, unusually large payments, and early-payment discounts that were missed or left unclaimed. Each one is explained on What It Checks, with an example.

  • How does Reclaim decide something is a mistake?

    It compares records against each other: vendors, amounts, invoice numbers, dates, and references. A finding is raised when the records themselves show the problem, and every finding lists the records it is based on.

  • Can a finding turn out to be fine?

    Yes. A partial payment, a deposit, or a credit applied outside your export can look like a mistake. That's why every finding shows its records, and why you review it before treating it as one.

  • Which accounting tools does it work with?

    Reclaim reads compatible CSV exports and supports sandbox testing for QuickBooks Online direct import. We have export guides for QuickBooks Online, Xero, NetSuite, and Bill.

  • Does Reclaim contact my vendors?

    Only once you approve a request, and then you send it from your Gmail or your own email. Reclaim keeps track of it, and you log the vendor’s replies on the finding.

  • How is my data handled?

    Our Security page covers what Reclaim reads, what it can never do, and how AI is kept to the minimum each task needs.

  • Who is Reclaim for?

    Businesses that pay a lot of vendors, without a team to chase every mistake: finance and AP teams, operators, and founders.

  • Never changes your books

    Reclaim works from the records you give it. It cannot move money or alter your ledger.

  • Nothing sent without you

    Every message to a vendor waits for your approval. Nothing reaches a vendor until you say so.

  • Refunds come to you

    Refunds and credits go straight to you. Reclaim never holds recovered funds.
